answers.explanation: Distance vector sends a number. Path vector sends the list of networks the route passes through.
It's distance vector with the path attached.
Seeing your own name in the path is how path vector prevents loops.
Policy is the big reason the Internet's inter-network routing is path vector.
Because a router can see itself in a looping path, it rejects the loop immediately.
The Border Gateway Protocol, coming up shortly.
Paths list autonomous systems, not routers. One AS might contain thousands of routers.
That's a business rule, not a distance. Path vector handles it; Bellman-Ford and Dijkstra can't.
